Modern.brandNameRationale: Single word, technical term. Circular is the economic model the category is built around: products designed to return to the system, not the landfill. The brand sits on the principle directly. No flowers. No earth-photographs.
Modern.industrySummary: Sustainability brands keep using nature imagery. Trees. Leaves. The earth from space. The category has run out of room in that direction. The opening is for brands that look like product companies and lead with design and engineering, not imagery.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Patagonia (patagonia.com) is the institution. Vollebak (vollebak.com) does material-science-led modern. Pangaia (thepangaia.com) sits at the design-meets-science intersection. We sit closer to Vollebak in posture, with sharper brand work.
Modern.positioningStatement: Sustainable products engineered to come back to the system.
Modern.positioningRationale: Most sustainability brands lean on imagery and storytelling. We lead with the engineering: the materials, the take-back program, the next life of every product. The proof is in the system, not the photography.

Modern.mission: To move food and consumer-goods companies from sustainability claims to sustainability operations.
Modern.vision: A consultancy whose published case studies are taught in supply-chain management programs.

Modern — sustainability as operations, not as marketing.

Anthesis Group (anthesisgroup.com) sits in the considered-modern peer middle. Climeworks Solutions (climeworks.com) plays the carbon-implementation peer reference. We belong alongside South Pole with a stronger regenerative-agriculture focus.
Modern.positioningStatement: Soil & Carbon is a sustainability consultancy specializing in regenerative agriculture transitions, carbon accounting, and supply-chain transparency.
Modern.positioningRationale: We compete on operational implementation rather than report production. Engagements end when the client operates differently, not when the report is delivered.

Luxury.vision: A foundation whose research is cited by the field for the next century.

Luxury.manifesto: Most environmental work runs on grant cycles and corporate-CSR timelines. The Wickwood Foundation was endowed in 1971 to support environmental research on the long arc. Corporate.brandDescription: Greenholt Environmental Holdings operates a portfolio of environmental services brands across waste management, soil remediation, water treatment, and ecological restoration categories.
Corporate.scope:
Greenholt Environmental Holdings works across:
• Multi-brand environmental services operations
• Shared regulatory compliance across jurisdictions
• Industrial and municipal contracts
• Capital-equipment procurement and management
• Annual investor and operator reporting
Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier environmental services brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: An environmental services operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the regulatory and capital infrastructure are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — regulatory compliance runs on schedule.
Reliable — capital-equipment capacity supports brand operations.
Discreet — brand and client relationships stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Greenholt is a constructed compound place-name (green + holt, where holt is the archaic English word for a small wood or grove) with a heritage holding-company register. Environmental Holdings follows the multi-brand operator naming convention used in environmental services (Veolia, Waste Management, Republic Services structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Greenholt Environmental Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of environmental services brands. Each brand retains its identity, technical leadership, and customer relationships; we operate the shared regulatory compliance, capital equipment, and back office. The buyer is a brand founder considering sale, a municipal procurement officer, an industrial client seeking consolidated supplier relationships, or an institutional investor holding environmental-services assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Environmental services has consolidated under a small number of large multi-brand operators (Veolia, Waste Management, Republic Services, Clean Harbors). The opening underneath is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator with deep compliance operations and the procurement-grade reliability municipal and industrial clients require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Veolia (veolia.com) is the multi-service environmental reference at scale. Republic Services (republicservices.com) holds the multi-category peer slot. Clean Harbors (cleanharbors.com) sits in the multi-service environmental peer position. Casella Waste Systems (casella.com) plays the regional peer reference. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand environmental-services operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Greenholt Environmental Holdings is a regional multi-brand environmental services operator running waste management, soil remediation, water treatment, and ecological restoration across a portfolio of brands.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared regulatory compliance, capital-equipment depth, and the procurement-grade reliability municipal and industrial clients require for multi-year operating relationships.

targetAudience.primary: Environmental services brand founders considering sale, municipal procurement officers, industrial clients consolidating environmental supplier relationships, and institutional investors holding environmental-services assets.
behaviors: Negotiate multi-year municipal and industrial contracts.
Care about regulatory compliance, capacity, and incident response.
motivations: Need an operator with shared regulatory compliance.
Need to keep brand identity post-acquisition.
Need a single-vendor multi-brand environmental-services relationship.

dos: Lead with brand portfolio, regulatory record, and capital-equipment footprint.
Speak the language of brand founders, municipal procurement, and industrial CFOs.
Publish quarterly operator letters.
Refer to brands by name, not by Greenholt tagging.
donts: No social media at the parent level.
No brand consolidation announcements without partner alignment.

Creative.tagline: A sustainability brand for the boring practical work.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Common Ground references both shared earth and shared political space. Project frames the work as ongoing. The naming follows the considered-creative environmental brand school.
Creative.manifesto: Most sustainability brands are too earnest to take seriously. They moralize. They scold. They make you feel bad. We made Nice Planet because climate work should be possible without becoming a different person. We're serious about the work. We're not serious about ourselves.
Creative.industrySummary: Sustainability branding has been earnest, beige, and slightly preachy. There's room for one that's loud, warm, full of personality, and still serious about the actual work. The category has been quiet for too long.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Allbirds (allbirds.com) does sustainability with restraint. Patagonia (patagonia.com) does it with conviction. Climate Town (the YouTube channel) does it with humor. We are closer to Climate Town in tone, applied to a brand and product company.
Creative.positioningStatement: A sustainability brand for people who want to do something without feeling guilty about the rest of their life.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Tries to do the right thing where it's easy. Already exhausted by climate-anxiety content. Wants to participate without joining a movement. Buys the totebag, reads the newsletter.

dos: Make jokes about the climate without minimizing it
Talk like a friend who reads the news
Tell the truth about what works and what doesn't

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with a slight smile curve under NICE. Standalone smiling-earth icon for stickers, social profiles, and packaging seals. The mark stays warm at every size.

colorPalette.name: Nice Green
colorPalette.usage: Primary brand color, hero surfaces, totebags

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and big display
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and labels
typography.rationale: Migra has personality and warmth. Neue Montreal handles the practical bits. The pair feels designed and friendly.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not earnest. Not preachy. Not afraid of green. Not too cool to make a joke about itself.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Totebags people actually use. Stickers in every order. A weekly newsletter that's mostly funny climate news. Pop-up events that are part education, part party. A merch line that's actually good. A printed zine three times a year.

Creative.tagline: A sustainability brand for the things you'd rather fix than replace.
Creative.brandDescription: The Mending Co is a creative-led sustainability brand operating a repair service for clothing, household goods, and small electronics, with a service-by-mail model and a published repair philosophy.
Creative.scope:
The Mending Co works across:
• Repair services for clothing, household goods, and small electronics
• Service-by-mail with prepaid return shipping
• Published repair-or-not assessments before work begins
• Quarterly published essays on the repair tradition
• Annual repair-club gatherings in three cities
Creative.mission: To make repair a normal household choice rather than a virtuous exception.
Creative.vision: A repair service whose mailroom queue is full of household objects on their second, third, and fourth life.
coreValues: Warm — repair is care for the things we own.
Specific — every assessment is written for the item.
Considered — some assessments recommend not repairing.
Literary — the writing about repair is part of the brand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Mending Co names the foundational repair practice — mending is the archaic verb for repairing clothing and small textile goods. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school. Stands in the lineage of declarative repair brands (Patagonia Worn Wear's spirit, iFixit's craft register, The Restory's repair tradition).
Creative.manifesto: Most household objects are designed to be replaced, not repaired. We started The Mending Co to make repair a normal household choice. Send us the garment, the lamp, the leather bag, the small appliance. We assess it. We give you an honest repair-or-not recommendation. If we repair it, we send it back with a printed repair record.
Creative.industrySummary: Repair services exist but are fragmented across cobblers, tailors, electronic repair shops, and small craft repair operations. There is real space for a creative-led brand that operates a multi-category repair service by mail with a clear philosophy and consistent quality.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Patagonia Worn Wear (patagonia.com/worn-wear) plays the closest peer in considered repair operations. The Restory (the-restory.com) holds the leather-and-luxury repair peer slot. iFixit (ifixit.com) sits in the electronics repair-tooling peer position. Rejean (rejeansjeans.com) plays the denim-repair peer reference. We sit alongside Patagonia Worn Wear with a multi-category by-mail model.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Mending Co is a multi-category repair service operating by mail, with a published repair philosophy and an honest repair-or-not assessment before any work begins.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the repair philosophy and on the honest assessment. Every item gets a written assessment before work begins; some assessments recommend not repairing the item.

targetAudience.primary: Households 30-55 with possessions they'd rather repair than replace — leather goods, well-made clothing, small electronics, household appliances.
behaviors: Own items they've kept for years and would like to keep longer.
Care about repair as a household practice.
Send items for repair when local options aren't available.
Want honest assessments about repair feasibility.
motivations: Want a repair service that handles multiple categories.
Want an honest assessment before paying for repair.
Want a brand that argues for repair as normal household practice.

dos: Publish the repair philosophy and assessment process.
Photograph repaired items before, during, and after.
Sign assessments by the lead repair specialist.
Reference completed repairs by item type and age in case studies.

messagingPillars.name: Multi-category repair
messagingPillars.description: We repair clothing, household goods (lamps, vases, small furniture), leather (bags, shoes, belts), and small electronics. The categories are the menu.

messagingPillars.name: Honest assessment
messagingPillars.description: Every item begins with a written assessment — what the repair would entail, what it would cost, whether it's worth doing. Some assessments recommend not repairing.

messagingPillars.name: Quarterly essay
messagingPillars.description: Once a quarter the brand publishes an essay on the repair tradition — history, craft, philosophy. The essay is the brand's primary marketing artefact.

Creative.tagline: A workshop for the things you fix yourself.
Creative.brandDescription: Tinker Workshop Co is a creative-led sustainability brand operating community repair workshops where members bring household objects to fix themselves under guided instruction.
Creative.scope:
Tinker Workshop Co works across:
• Community repair workshops for household objects
• Guided instruction from named makers
• Tool libraries available to workshop members
• Quarterly published essays on the tinker tradition
• Annual tinker gathering
Creative.mission: To restore the practice of fixing one's own things in community.
Creative.vision: A workshop whose members repair their own household objects across years.
coreValues: Warm — fixing is community work.
Specific — every repair is taught.
Considered — the workshop is the brand.
Literary — the writing about tinkering is part of the work.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Tinker is the archaic word for a travelling mender of household objects — single trade word with deep heritage in repair tradition. Workshop is the plain working-space suffix. Co is the small-firm convention.
Creative.manifesto: Most sustainability brands sell products. We started Tinker Workshop Co because the actual most sustainable practice is fixing what you already own — and the actual most useful sustainability space is a workshop where you do that.
Creative.industrySummary: Sustainability is marketed through products. There is real space for a brand that operates community repair workshops.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Repair Cafés (repaircafe.org) play the heritage community repair peer. iFixit (ifixit.com) holds the educational repair peer slot. The Mending Co (within the catalog) plays the peer reference. We sit alongside Repair Cafés with a commercial workshop model.
Creative.positioningStatement: Tinker Workshop Co is a sustainability brand operating community repair workshops where members fix household objects under guided instruction.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the community-workshop premise.

behaviors: Pay for instruction and tool access.
motivations: Want community repair workshops.
Want guided instruction.
Want tool library access.
